lanes.source_family: National statistics: NBS monthly energy production releases (能源生产情况), read for production effects explicitly attributed to a disruption
registry: NBS Statistical Communiqué and monthly energy releases
lanes.finding: Substantive negative finding: across all 53 releases (data months 2021-12 to 2026-09) the NBS energy production release never attributes a production change to a disruption. No release mentions an accident, flood, typhoon, drought or water inflow, weather, shutdown, power rationing, or maintenance, and no release gives a province-level figure: all figures are national totals for above-scale industry. The only causal wording found is supply-policy language attached to coal growth in six releases (data months 2021-12, 2022-03, 2022-04, 2022-05, 2022-06, 2022-11: for example 增产保供政策持续推进, 煤炭保供稳价政策深入推进, 为做好今冬保暖保供工作), plus a days-adjustment phrase for power generation (扣除天数原因) in data months 2025-03 to 2025-08 and a recurring comparability footnote. From 2022-12 onward the text is purely descriptive. Large swings are reported with no stated cause, for example hydro generation -30.0% in 2022-09, -32.9% in 2023-05 and -22.9% for the first half of 2023. This source family therefore cannot yield candidates under any clause, and an unexplained change in it must not be read as evidence of a disruption.
lanes.limitation: Nothing in the universe is unread, but each page was read through WebFetch, which returns a model's reading of the page rather than the raw text; the model declined to reproduce full bodies, so the per-release result rests on its answer to a fixed question asking for every causal phrase verbatim. The attached Excel data tables were not opened. The October 2026 release is not yet published.

lanes.source_family: National Energy Administration and grid companies (State Grid, China Southern Grid): notices of major outages, orderly power use, emergency responses
registry: State Grid and China Southern Grid notices
lanes.finding: The NEA safety department's own listing is the one fully read source here and it is almost silent on events: of 275 titles in the window, 3 concern an actual outage (Gansu earthquake Dec 2023, two items; Hebei Zhuozhou floods Aug 2023) and 1 names an event (Xinjiang 3 Aug 2024 oscillation) without stating any effect. The monthly 事故通报 and 全国电力安全生产情况 series on that listing stop in 2021 (last: Oct 2021 data, published 2021-11-30); nothing in the window replaces them. The site: operator is ignored by the search tool; allowed_domains works for nea.gov.cn, csg.cn and sgcc.com.cn and returned operator pages. Planned demand management seen and logged apart, not as candidates: none on NEA/CSG/SGCC pages in this lane.
lanes.limitation: State Grid's site did not respond and NEA's general news listing is script-only, so both are unread; China Southern Grid's company-news archive is reachable (20 items a page, paged as index_N.html, by year) but only 3 pages (60 titles) were sampled, and none of the 15 year queries ran before the shared search limit was hit. No English query is declared in the plan and none was run, so the zh+en requirement is not met.

lanes.source_family: Provincial outage and disruption reporting: provincial energy bureaus and government notices of power rationing or grid emergencies
lanes.finding: Yield was plans, not disruptions. Logged apart as planned demand management or standing rules, never as candidates: Guangzhou 2026 load-management plan and 2021 orderly-power-use plan; Laizhou (Shandong) 2026 summer load-management plan; Inner Mongolia Mengxi/Mengdong orderly-power-use plans (2021, 2022, 2023 editions) and league-level plans; Xinjiang load-management rules (2024); Jiangsu 2024 load-management notice and 2026 electricity-saving notice; Zhejiang 2019 plan; Henan 2020 plan and 2022 supply notice. Provincial NEA office pages migrated in 2023 carry 2023 dates in their URLs but describe older events (Henan Jan 2018, Zhejiang summer 2013); the search summary presented the Zhejiang 2013 event as 2023. Any record built from these subdomains needs the on-page date. One result surfaced for Inner Mongolia was the 2023 Alxa mine collapse already in the corpus (not a grid event, not counted as a candidate).
lanes.limitation: A declared query set, not a census: each query returned about 10 results and only 5 result pages were opened; provincial energy-bureau notice listings were not enumerated. The 'P 大面积停电 应急响应 政府' query returns emergency plans (预案) for almost every province, often from other provinces, and is a poor instrument for finding events.

lanes.source_family: Major state enterprises (Sinopec, PetroChina, CNOOC, China Shenhua, State Power Investment): HKEX and SSE announcements of facility incidents or production susp
registry: State energy enterprise exchange announcements (Sinopec, PetroChina, CNOOC, China Shenhua, SPIC)
lanes.finding: The generic declared queries return mainly pre-2022 events, planned maintenance and share-trading halts (停牌), which the search engine conflates with 停产. No accepted candidate. Two held: CNOOC Lingshui 17-2 field shutdown in 2026 (no volume, no event date) and Guodian Power's Chahasu coal mine regulatory halt, 2023 (filing opened). Unopened leads not made into candidates because no date or page could be read: a report that Sinopec cut refining runs during a Strait of Hormuz crude-supply disruption in 2026 (tankterminals page 404; a supply-driven run cut, lead should decide whether clause 1 can apply at all); unplanned petrochemical-unit stops at Sinopec Qilu (Dec 2023) and PetroChina Liaoyang (Feb 2024), which are chemical units, not refining throughput. The miningweekly 2023-05-09 '50Mt halted' item (403) is probably the aftermath of the Alxa collapse already in the corpus; unverified.
lanes.limitation: The notice archives themselves were not enumerated: HKEX and SSE listings are interactive or script-only, and of the five company notice pages only PetroChina's was reachable, showing its 20 most recent titles (2026-04-29 to 2026-11-05, all routine governance, none about a suspension) with no visible pagination. Annual-report PDFs were not opened. All 15 declared queries ran in both languages, but they are a keyword probe of an archive lane, not a reading of it.

lanes.source_family: Credible Chinese-language media: Xinhua, People's Daily, Caixin, The Paper
registry: Chinese national media (Xinhua, People's Daily, Caixin, The Paper)
lanes.finding: No new qualifying event. Plain refinery queries return foreign refineries almost exclusively; domain-restricted reruns return Xinhua world-desk copy on foreign refineries plus the three domestic events already in the corpus. Coal queries return a recurring pattern in The Paper: listed-company notices of single-mine halts after one-fatality accidents, stating approved capacity but no lost volume (the one stated loss was about 90,000 t). Gas-pipeline queries return only urban distribution incidents (Yanjiao 2024, Anping 2023) and events outside the window (Shiyan 2021, Qinglong) or outside China; no domestic trunk-pipeline shutdown surfaced. 'examined' is an approximate count of result items across 18 searches.
lanes.limitation: A 15-string query set through a general search engine is not a search of the four outlets' archives: Caixin returned no result in any of the 18 searches and People's Daily only a handful, so lane credit rests almost entirely on The Paper and Xinhua. No outlet site search was run, and named-event follow-ups (Zhenhai January 2025, held in pass 17) were not possible within the cap.

lanes.source_family: International corroboration: Reuters, Bloomberg, S&P Global reporting of Chinese energy disruptions
registry: International news agencies and energy press (Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, S&P Global, Argus)
lanes.finding: English wire coverage of Chinese power rationing found no firm load shed after 2023: results for 2024, 2025 and 2026 report record demand and renewable curtailment, not rationing. English refinery-fire coverage for 2022-2026 returned only events already in the corpus plus one commissioning fire and one walled headline. Coal-accident coverage is dense but almost never states a supply cut in tonnes; trade press (Mysteel) states halted capacity, behind a login wall.
lanes.limitation: All 15 declared English queries ran and were dispositioned, but this is a query set, not a census, and the wire syndication sites carrying most Reuters and Bloomberg coal stories (mining.com, miningweekly, engineeringnews) refused access, so those articles were judged from headlines. Three held candidates had no Chinese-language follow-up because the 22-search cap was reached. Seen in result lists and not pursued: 2024 Shanxi safety-inspection output curbs (a regulatory campaign, not a discrete event), two mine accidents of 23 Oct 2024 in Hebei and Shanxi, and a reported 2024 output fall in one Heilongjiang city.
